Ehsan Suez, PhD
ResearchTeachingPublicationsCV

I use computational and statistical methods to study infectious disease dynamics, improve epidemic forecasting, and support public health decision-making. My research spans infectious disease modeling, outbreak analytics, probabilistic forecasting, and model evaluation.

I am currently a Steven M. Teutsch Prevention Effectiveness Fellow at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), working in the Center for Forecasting and Outbreak Analytics (CFA), where I focus on infectious disease modeling and outbreak analytics.

I received my PhD in Bioinformatics from the University of Georgia in 2026, working with Spencer J. Fox . My doctoral research focused on improving infectious disease forecasting through baseline benchmarking, scenario-informed forecasting, and collaborative forecasting systems. I also earned a Graduate Certificate in Public Health from the University of Georgia in 2024. Previously, I earned an MS in Biology from Missouri State University and a BSc in Biotechnology and Genetic Engineering from Jahangirnagar University.

You can read more about my research, publications, and teaching, or browse my CV.
